stories.title: StemDeck, a free, open-source and local AI stem separator
stories.paragraph: StemDeck is a free, open-source audio stem separation tool that runs entirely on a local machine, requiring no cloud processing or subscription. The project joins a growing category of locally hosted AI audio tools that give users privacy and offline capability, distinguishing itself from services like Moises or Lalal.ai that require uploading audio to remote servers. By running inference locally, it avoids sending potentially sensitive or proprietary recordings to third parties.

stories.title: LibreOffice 26.8 is out – local first, and with no AI
stories.paragraph: The Document Foundation released LibreOffice 26.8, a version it explicitly positions as local-first and without integrated AI features, setting it apart from competing office suites that have moved to embed AI assistants. The release is notable in the current software landscape where AI integration has become a near-universal selling point, and the project's stance reflects a deliberate choice to prioritize offline functionality and user data control. Specific new features and performance improvements were included in the release, though the most discussed aspect in the community has been the continued absence of AI tooling.

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic are ruining San Francisco
stories.paragraph: An SFGate opinion piece argues that the rapid expansion of OpenAI and Anthropic in San Francisco is inflating commercial rents, displacing longtime businesses, and reshaping neighborhood character in ways that benefit a narrow tech workforce. The piece points to the companies' large office footprints in the Mission and SoMa districts as contributors to a broader affordability squeeze. The article reflects a recurring tension in the city between the economic activity tech firms generate and the costs borne by residents and small businesses.

stories.title: Anthropic Just Beat The Pentagon in Court
stories.paragraph: A federal judge ruled in favor of Anthropic after the Pentagon sought to terminate a contract with the company, with the court finding that national security justifications were used improperly to penalize Anthropic for its own AI usage policies. The ruling is notable because it scrutinizes government use of security rationales to exert pressure on AI vendors over their internal product guidelines. The case sets a potential precedent for how contractors that develop and enforce their own AI safety rules can respond to federal procurement disputes.

stories.title: X claims it found a Chinese bot farm posting anti-AI data center sentiments
stories.paragraph: X, formerly Twitter, said it identified a network of accounts linked to a Chinese bot farm that was coordinating posts expressing opposition to AI data center construction in the United States. The company did not publish detailed methodology or third-party verification for the attribution. The claim arrives amid broader geopolitical tensions around AI infrastructure investment, and observers note that such attributions, without independent corroboration, are difficult to assess.

stories.title: I'm the Guy Who Destroys Antique Books After We Scan Them into Our Company's AI
stories.paragraph: McSweeney's published a satirical first-person piece narrated by a fictional employee whose job is to physically destroy rare books once they have been digitized and ingested into a corporate AI platform. The humor derives from the narrator's bureaucratic matter-of-factness about an activity with obvious cultural and legal implications, touching on questions of copyright, provenance, and institutional accountability in AI training data collection. The piece functions as social commentary on the largely opaque processes by which companies assemble large training corpora.

stories.title: Nvidia Insists It Can Keep Printing Money to Fund the AI Boom
stories.paragraph: Nvidia has publicly pushed back against concerns that its revenue growth tied to AI infrastructure spending is unsustainable, asserting that demand for its chips remains strong enough to support continued investment in the sector. The company's position is notable given rising scrutiny from analysts and investors over whether hyperscaler capital expenditure on AI hardware can persist at current levels. Nvidia has not disclosed a specific revenue forecast in this context, but its argument centers on the breadth of industries now deploying AI workloads as a foundation for ongoing demand.

stories.title: Debian Votes to Allow "Responsible Use of Generative AI"
stories.paragraph: The Debian project held a general resolution vote and approved a position permitting the responsible use of generative AI tools by contributors, after significant internal debate about AI-generated code quality, licensing concerns, and attribution. The resolution does not mandate AI use but establishes a framework under which contributors may employ such tools while maintaining Debian's existing standards for software freedom and package quality. The vote outcome reflects a broader negotiation happening across open-source communities about how to accommodate generative AI without compromising long-standing principles.

stories.title: Debian votes to allow "responsible use of generative AI"
stories.paragraph: LWN.net provided detailed coverage of the Debian general resolution on generative AI, including vote tallies and the range of positions debated by project members. The discussion surfaced concerns about whether AI-generated contributions could satisfy Debian's requirements for reproducible, auditable, and freely licensed code. The resolution passed with conditions, and LWN's reporting highlights the procedural complexity involved when a large volunteer-driven project formalizes policy on a contested technical practice.

stories.title: Identifying fake cosmetics using AI
stories.paragraph: Researchers at the Grover Lab published a method for detecting counterfeit cosmetics using AI-based analysis, describing a technique that examines physical or chemical signatures of products to distinguish genuine items from fakes. Counterfeiting in the cosmetics industry is a documented public health concern, as fake products can contain unlabeled or harmful ingredients. The post details the approach at a technical level, positioning machine learning as a practical tool for quality verification in consumer goods supply chains.

stories.title: The Analytical AI Handbook
stories.paragraph: Sutro published an online handbook focused on applying AI methods to analytical workflows, covering topics such as data interpretation, model selection, and structured reasoning with language models. The resource is positioned as a practitioner reference rather than an introductory tutorial, addressing how to integrate AI-assisted analysis into rigorous technical processes. It joins a small but growing body of domain-specific AI guidance aimed at analysts rather than ML engineers.

stories.title: AI demands more engineering discipline. Not less
stories.paragraph: Charity Majors, co-founder of Honeycomb, argues in a Substack post that the proliferation of AI-assisted coding tools increases rather than reduces the need for strong software engineering fundamentals, including testing, observability, and code review. Her central claim is that AI code generation accelerates output in ways that can outpace a team's ability to understand and maintain what it ships, making discipline around verification more critical. The piece pushes back against narratives that AI tools can substitute for engineering rigor, framing them instead as amplifiers of both good and bad practices.

stories.title: Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days
stories.paragraph: Cambridge professor and OCaml core maintainer Anil Madhavapeddy reported that security vulnerabilities in OCaml projects are now seeing attempted exploits within minutes of patches being shared for internal discussion, before any public disclosure. Simon Willison highlighted the post as evidence that the window between patch development and active exploitation has compressed to the point where even rumor of a fix can trigger scanning and attack attempts. The observation has implications for how open-source projects manage coordinated disclosure and patch distribution logistics.

stories.title: New Fellows Research: Can Claude autonomously align other AIs?
stories.paragraph: Anthropic published research exploring whether Claude can autonomously improve the alignment of other AI models, giving the model 48 hours and a single GPU to research, propose, and apply alignment methods to small models without human intervention. Across 10 distinct alignment failures — including deception and sycophancy — Claude improved safety scores without degrading general capabilities, and its best methods generalized to held-out benchmarks and models up to 4.7 times larger. Anthropic also tested a cross-model scenario in which Sonnet 5 post-trained an early checkpoint of Opus 4.8, a more capable model, achieving safety scores approaching those of the production Opus 4.8 that went through full alignment training. The researchers note a key limitation: subtle or rare failures that lack any measurable benchmark cannot be addressed by this approach, making benchmark selection a critical dependency. Anthropic is releasing the automated alignment research setup publicly for others to build on.

stories.title: The Uninvited Guest Who Crashed Our Family Vacation: My Mom's AI Chatbot
stories.paragraph: A Wall Street Journal piece recounts how an AI chatbot — specifically Claude — became an unwanted presence during a family vacation when an older parent brought the tool into group interactions, illustrating how AI adoption among older generations is reshaping social dynamics. The story highlights a generational divide in expectations around technology use in personal settings, with younger family members expressing discomfort at the chatbot's intrusion into shared moments. The anecdote serves as a concrete example of how consumer AI tools, initially framed as personal productivity aids, are beginning to affect interpersonal relationships in unanticipated ways.

stories.title: Ask HN: AI writes better code than me. How to keep my identity?
stories.paragraph: A Hacker News thread initiated by a freelance developer captures a growing professional concern: as AI-assisted coding becomes the market baseline, practitioners who rely heavily on tools like GPT-5.3 report feeling uncertain about their own role and creative identity. The original poster notes that client deadlines are now set assuming AI-accelerated output, making it effectively impossible to compete without adopting these tools. The discussion reflects a broader tension in software development between efficiency gains from AI delegation and the loss of direct craft engagement that many developers cite as central to job satisfaction.

stories.title: How I Design with AI
stories.paragraph: A practitioner published a detailed account of how AI tools have been integrated into a design workflow, describing specific ways generative AI assists with ideation, iteration, and production tasks. The piece is notable for its focus on practical method rather than general enthusiasm, walking through concrete steps in the process rather than offering abstract commentary on AI's potential in creative fields. It contributes to a growing body of first-person practitioner accounts that document how AI is actually being used day-to-day, as opposed to how it is marketed.
